questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut opens the integrated terminal in VS Code?
questions.why: It opens the terminal inside VS Code.

questions.q: What does the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) do?
options: Runs any VS Code action when you type its name
questions.why: Type what you want and VS Code finds the action.

questions.q: In a terminal, what does pwd show you?
questions.why: pwd prints the working directory.

questions.q: What does npm install do?
options: Installs the packages a project lists in package.json
questions.why: It reads package.json and installs what the project needs.

questions.q: Copilot shows grey suggestion text. How do you accept and dismiss it?
options: Tab to accept, Esc to dismiss
Enter to accept, Delete to dismiss
Ctrl+S to accept, Ctrl+Z to dismiss
questions.why: Tab accepts ghost text and Esc dismisses it.

questions.q: Why read Copilot's code before relying on it?
options: It can be wrong or incomplete
questions.why: AI suggests, you review: it can miss cases or be wrong.

questions.q: Which command runs a Playwright test suite?
questions.why: It runs every test in the project.

questions.q: Which prompt is better for Copilot, A: Write a test. or B: On /checkout, write a test that checks the total changes when the quantity changes.
options: B: On /checkout, write a test that checks the total changes when the quantity changes.
questions.why: B names the page, the action and the expected result.

questions.q: In an automated test, what is the difference between a selector and an assertion?
options: A selector finds an element, an assertion checks the result
An assertion finds an element, a selector checks the result
questions.why: Find the thing, then check what it shows.

questions.q: Which tool records your clicks and turns them into a starting test?
questions.why: Codegen records a flow and writes a first test you then improve.

cards.title: Git for New Testers
cards.imageAlt: Title card: Git for New Testers
cards.summary: A tester who has never used version control learns to save, branch, share and fix a conflict with eight commands. Four sessions of 30 minutes.
cards.visualAlt: Looping illustration: a branch leaves the main line, gets two commits, and returns through a pull request while main stays safe.
cards.code: I changed tests/login.spec.ts and want a teammate to review it. Give me the Git commands in order, and say what each one does in everyday words.
cards.oneLiner: Four 30-minute sessions and eight commands take a tester from no version control to a pull request.

quiz.passMessage: Ready to work on a real project.
quiz.failMessage: Go back over the four sessions, then try again.

questions.q: What does a commit do?
options: Sends your files to a teammate
Saves a snapshot of your changes with a message
questions.why: A commit is a save point you can return to.

questions.q: Why work on a branch instead of main?
options: Git does not allow commits on main
Main stays working while you try your change
questions.why: Nothing reaches main until someone has reviewed it.

questions.q: Which command starts a new branch and moves you onto it?
questions.why: The -c means create.

questions.q: What does git add do?
options: Chooses which changes go into the next commit
questions.why: You can add some files and leave others for later.

questions.q: What does git push do?
options: Brings your teammates’ changes to your computer
Copies your branch’s commits to GitHub
questions.why: Until you push, nobody else can see your work.

questions.q: What is a pull request?
options: A request to download the project
A request for a teammate to review your branch and merge it
A command that undoes a commit
questions.why: It is where the discussion happens.

questions.q: Git says CONFLICT in a file. What happened?
options: You and a teammate changed the same lines, and you choose what stays
questions.why: Git will not guess which change is right.

questions.q: Which file should never be committed?
options: A file with a password or key in it
questions.why: Once pushed, a secret stays in the history.

questions.q: A fix is ready and the ticket is In Test. Whose turn is it?
questions.why: The developer has handed it over.

questions.q: Which part of a bug ticket do testers most often leave out?
questions.why: Without it, nobody knows what counts as a bug.

questions.q: A retest still fails. What do you do?
options: Move it to Reopened and add what still fails
Open a second ticket for the same bug
Move it to Done and mention it in chat
questions.why: Do not open a second ticket for the same bug.

questions.q: Why attach evidence?
options: It makes the ticket look longer
So the developer can see the bug without asking
questions.why: A screenshot or recording saves a round trip.

questions.q: What does this query find? project = HBL AND status = "In Test"
options: Every ticket in the Harbourline project
Tickets in the Harbourline project that are waiting for a tester
questions.why: The query reads like a sentence: this project, in this status.

questions.q: You moved a ticket to Done, then found a new bug nearby. What now?
options: Raise a new ticket and link it
Reopen the old ticket and add the new bug
Add the new bug to the Done ticket’s comments
questions.why: A closed ticket should describe one fix.
